title: AP Calculus BC
units: Differentiation: Composite, Implicit, and Inverse Functions
Parametric Equations, Polar Coordinates, and Vector-Valued Functions

activities.title: Removable discontinuities
activities.description: Approach a missing point while separating f(a) from the limit.
activities.limits: A factored rational family; the original expression is undefined at a. The graph explicitly marks the hole.
activities.goal: Explain why a limit can exist even when the function value is missing.

activities.title: One-sided limits & jumps
activities.description: Change left and right limits independently.
activities.equation: A two-sided limit exists only if both one-sided limits agree.
activities.limits: Piecewise constant example, with separately defined f(0).
activities.goal: Distinguish function value, one-sided limits and the two-sided limit.

activities.title: Squeeze theorem & oscillation
activities.description: Bound an oscillating function near zero.
activities.limits: Set the value at 0 to 0 for plotting; rapid oscillations below sample resolution are not resolved.
activities.goal: Justify a limit using bounds rather than visual smoothness.

activities.title: Intermediate value theorem
activities.description: Test a target against endpoint values of a continuous cubic.
activities.equation: Continuous f on [a,b] takes every value between f(a) and f(b).
activities.limits: f(x)=x³−3x. Endpoint bracketing guarantees existence, not uniqueness. Lack of bracketing does not establish nonexistence.
activities.goal: State hypotheses and distinguish a guarantee from a guess.

activities.title: Secants & the derivative limit
activities.description: Shrink a secant interval and compare its slope with an analytic derivative.
activities.limits: Preset functions only. h cannot be zero; derivatives are analytic rather than inferred from tiny floating-point differences.
activities.goal: Explain what changes and what remains fixed as h approaches zero.

activities.title: Tangent lines & local behavior
activities.description: Move along a cubic and compare the tangent with the curve.
activities.limits: f(x)=x³−3x; the tangent is local, not a global replacement for the curve.
activities.goal: Explain why equal values at the tangency point do not imply equal values elsewhere.

activities.title: Product rule
activities.description: Compare the derivative of x²sin(bx) to both contributing terms.
activities.limits: All trigonometric inputs are in radians. Neither factor is treated as constant.
activities.goal: Explain why multiplying two derivatives is not the product rule.

activities.title: Quotient rule
activities.description: Investigate the derivative of x/(x²+c) with a positive denominator parameter.
activities.limits: c>0, so the chosen denominator never vanishes for real x.
activities.goal: Explain why the sign of the derivative can change even when the denominator is positive.

activities.title: Chain rule & composition
activities.description: Differentiate sin(bx²) and track the inner derivative.
activities.limits: Angles in radians; x range is bounded to display multiple oscillations.
activities.goal: Explain why the outer derivative must be multiplied by the inner derivative.

activities.title: Implicit differentiation
activities.description: Locate a circle point and calculate its tangent slope on a selected branch.
activities.limits: At x=±r the tangent is vertical and a finite dy/dx does not exist. This explorer requires |x|<r.
activities.goal: Explain why solving for y is not required to differentiate implicitly.

activities.title: Inverse functions & derivative
activities.description: Compare a monotone exponential with its logarithmic inverse.
activities.limits: f is one-to-one for b>0; logarithm input must be positive.
activities.goal: Explain why derivatives of inverse functions are evaluated at related points.

activities.title: Higher derivatives & concavity
activities.description: Connect cubic function, first derivative and second derivative.
activities.limits: Continuous polynomial family. Concavity concerns how f′ changes, not whether f is positive.
activities.goal: Distinguish decreasing from concave down using both derivatives.

activities.title: Position, velocity & acceleration
activities.description: Interpret a polynomial position model and locate instantaneous rates.
activities.limits: One-dimensional ideal motion; signs describe direction, not speed magnitude.
activities.goal: Explain when an object speeds up using velocity and acceleration signs.

activities.title: Related rates: expanding sphere
activities.description: Relate a radius rate to volume rate at one instant.
activities.limits: Sphere geometry with instantaneous supplied radius rate. A constant radius rate does not give a constant volume rate.
activities.goal: Explain why the current radius is needed as well as its rate.

activities.title: Linear approximation
activities.description: Approximate a square root near a positive base point and compare the exact value.
activities.limits: Uses a local tangent approximation; the exact square root remains defined for these bounds.
activities.goal: Explain how error changes as the target moves away from the base point.

activities.title: L’Hôpital’s rule & indeterminate limits
activities.description: Compare a 0/0 family with its derivative ratio near zero.
activities.limits: Requires the 0/0 form and valid derivative-ratio limit; direct substitution alone does not give the limit. Radians are required.
activities.goal: State the indeterminate form before applying a rule.

activities.title: Mean value theorem
activities.description: Locate the point whose tangent slope equals an interval’s secant slope.
activities.limits: Continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b). Only the quadratic family is solved here.
activities.goal: Explain why both MVT hypotheses are needed.

activities.title: Critical points & sign analysis
activities.description: Use the derivative’s sign to classify a cubic’s stationary points.
activities.limits: For b<0 there are two stationary points; b=0 is a stationary inflection; b>0 has none.
activities.goal: Explain why f′=0 alone does not establish a local extremum.

activities.title: Absolute extrema on an interval
activities.description: Compare endpoints and interior critical points rather than checking only stationary points.
activities.equation: Candidates are endpoints and interior critical points.
activities.limits: f=x³−3x is continuous; the closed interval guarantees attained extrema.
activities.goal: Explain why endpoints must be checked even when their derivatives are not zero.

activities.title: Optimization: open-top box
activities.description: Change a corner cut and locate maximum volume for a rectangular sheet.
activities.limits: Cuts require 0<x<min(L,W)/2. Thin sheet, no material thickness or construction constraints.
activities.goal: Derive a function, state its domain and justify the maximum.

activities.title: Riemann sums
activities.description: Compare left, right and midpoint rectangle approximations with an exact definite integral.
activities.limits: Equal-width rectangles; preset analytic functions. Signed contributions are retained.
activities.goal: Explain over- and under-estimation using monotonicity, not a memorized universal rule.

activities.title: Accumulation & the FTC
activities.description: Explore A(x)=∫₀ˣ(t²−c)dt and connect its slope to the integrand.
activities.limits: Variable upper limit may be negative; orientation determines the sign of accumulation.
activities.goal: Explain why an accumulation function can decrease even when its value is positive.

activities.title: FTC with a composite upper bound
activities.description: Differentiate an integral whose upper endpoint is x².
activities.limits: Angles in radians; the accumulation function is 1−cos(x²).
activities.goal: Explain why simply substituting x² into the integrand is incomplete.

activities.title: Definite integration & substitution
activities.description: Transform ∫2x cos(x²)dx and preserve the definite bounds.
activities.limits: Signed definite integral; reversed bounds are allowed and negate the result.
activities.goal: Explain why bounds must change when the integration variable changes.

activities.title: Slope fields & solution curves
activities.description: Compare local slopes y′=x−y with a solution through an initial point.
activities.limits: Analytic solution of y′=x−y; the slope-field marks are local directions, not finite changes.
activities.goal: Explain how the same differential equation has many solution curves.

activities.title: Separable differential equations
activities.description: Compare solution values for y′=xy after an initial condition selects a constant.
activities.limits: Positive initial value; the identically zero solution also exists but is not included in these controls.
activities.goal: Explain why division by y requires attention to a possible zero solution.

activities.title: Exponential differential equations
activities.description: Model growth or decay from a constant relative rate.
activities.limits: Constant rate and no resource limit or source term; time units must match k.
activities.goal: Explain the distinction between constant relative rate and constant absolute rate.

activities.title: Verifying a differential-equation solution
activities.description: Substitute a candidate y=Ce^(ax) into y′=ky.
activities.limits: For nonzero C, the candidate solves the equation for all x only if a=k. One numerical point alone is not a proof.
activities.goal: Explain why checking a derivative is stronger than checking only an initial value.

activities.title: Displacement & total distance
activities.description: Split a linear velocity integral at a direction change.
activities.limits: One-dimensional motion. Integrals are evaluated analytically using the antiderivative of |t−c|.
activities.goal: Explain why total distance can exceed displacement magnitude.

activities.title: Area between curves
activities.description: Use the correct upper-minus-lower integrand between two intersections.
activities.equation: Area between y=H−x² and y=0 is 4H^(3/2)/3
activities.limits: The full bounded region is between x=−√H and x=√H. Area is nonnegative.
activities.goal: Explain how intersections determine bounds.

activities.title: Disks & washers
activities.description: Compare rotational cross-section area with region height.
activities.limits: Constant-radius annular solid over the interval. Real variable-radius problems require functions inside the integral.
activities.goal: Explain why squaring a difference of radii is not the washer area.

activities.title: Average value of a function
activities.description: Compare an integral’s total with its interval-normalized average.
activities.limits: Continuous preset families; an average value is not necessarily the midpoint function value.
activities.goal: Explain why dividing by interval length is required.

activities.title: Integration by parts
activities.description: Evaluate ∫xeˣdx and compare the boundary term with the remaining integral.
activities.limits: BC topic; definite integral preserves bound orientation.
activities.goal: Justify a choice of u and dv that simplifies the remaining integral.

activities.title: Partial fractions
activities.description: Decompose a rational integrand with distinct linear factors.
activities.limits: BC topic; distinct positive a and b keep poles outside [0,end].
activities.goal: Explain why a rational decomposition can make integration simpler.

activities.title: Improper integrals & convergence
activities.description: Compare finite cutoffs with the infinite integral of x^(−p).
activities.limits: BC topic. A finite positive cutoff always gives finite area, which alone does not establish convergence.
activities.goal: Distinguish a large finite approximation from a convergent improper integral.

activities.title: Euler’s method
activities.description: Compare numerical steps with the exact solution of y′=x+y.
activities.limits: BC topic; forward Euler with uniform steps. Longer times and larger steps can yield large errors.
activities.goal: Explain why each step uses a local tangent approximation.

activities.title: Logistic differential equations
activities.description: Locate the inflection population and compare initial and limiting growth.
activities.limits: BC topic; closed population with constant positive r and K, no age structure or time delay.
activities.goal: Explain why total growth peaks at K/2.

activities.title: Arc length of a graph
activities.description: Approximate the length of y=x² over an interval.
activities.limits: BC topic; Simpson numerical integration with 1000 panels. This is length, not area.
activities.goal: Explain the origin of the square root using small line segments.

activities.title: Parametric derivatives
activities.description: Analyze x=t, y=at² and distinguish parameter rate from slope.
activities.limits: BC-only unit. Here dx/dt=1 so all tangent slopes are finite.
activities.goal: Explain why dy/dt alone is not generally a slope in the xy-plane.

activities.title: Parametric ellipse & vertical tangents
activities.description: Change ellipse radii and evaluate a tangent at a parameter angle.
activities.equation: x=a cos t, y=b sin t; dy/dx=−b cos t/(a sin t)
activities.limits: BC-only unit. The displayed slope is undefined where sin t=0; no finite slope should be assigned there.
activities.goal: Distinguish a vertical tangent from a breakdown of the parametric curve.

activities.title: Vector-valued motion
activities.description: Calculate speed and acceleration for r(t)=⟨t,at²⟩.
activities.limits: BC-only unit. Coordinate units are meters and parameter units seconds for this ideal path.
activities.goal: Explain why speed is a magnitude rather than the sum of velocity components.

activities.title: Parametric arc length
activities.description: Integrate speed along an ellipse rather than using graph width.
activities.limits: BC-only unit. Numerical Simpson integration with 1000 panels over t=0 to the chosen endpoint.
activities.goal: Explain why different coordinate speeds contribute quadratically.

activities.title: Polar curves & traced area
activities.description: Change a rose curve and integrate area over a specified parameter interval.
activities.limits: BC-only unit. Integrating over an interval that retraces the curve counts area with multiplicity, not necessarily unique enclosed area.
activities.goal: Explain why negative r does not make the area integrand negative.

activities.title: Polar tangents
activities.description: Differentiate r=a(1+cos θ) using Cartesian coordinate derivatives.
activities.limits: BC-only unit. Cusp and vertical-tangent cases require separate analysis; finite slope checks exclude near-zero dx/dθ.
activities.goal: Explain why dr/dθ is not dy/dx.

activities.title: Geometric series & partial sums
activities.description: Compare partial sums with a convergent infinite geometric series.
activities.limits: BC-only unit. Infinite-sum convergence is conditional on |r|<1 for a nonzero first term.
activities.goal: Explain why terms approaching zero is necessary but not sufficient for general series convergence.

activities.title: p-series & the integral test
activities.description: Compare finite sums and tail bounds for Σ1/nᵖ.
activities.limits: BC-only unit. For p>1, ∫N+1∞f≤tail≤∫N∞f. Bounds require positive decreasing f.
activities.goal: Explain why a finite partial sum never proves convergence.

activities.title: Alternating series & error bounds
activities.description: Compare an alternating harmonic partial sum with ln 2.
activities.limits: BC-only unit. Error bound uses positive decreasing term magnitudes tending to zero; this series is conditionally convergent.
activities.goal: Explain how an alternating-series bound differs from its exact error.

activities.title: Ratio test & factorial terms
activities.description: Apply the ratio test to Σxⁿ/n! and compare its partial sum with eˣ.
activities.limits: BC-only unit. Terms start at n=0; the series converges absolutely for every finite real x.
activities.goal: Explain why a ratio limit of zero establishes convergence.

activities.title: Taylor polynomials for eˣ
activities.description: Compare a centered Taylor polynomial with its function and a Lagrange bound.
activities.limits: BC-only unit. M=e^max(a,x) bounds the next derivative on the interval between a and x.
activities.goal: Explain why the polynomial center and target distance both matter.

activities.title: Maclaurin polynomials for sin x
activities.description: Increase the number of nonzero terms while preserving odd powers.
activities.limits: BC-only unit. The series converges for every finite x; small-degree approximations can be poor far from zero.
activities.goal: Explain why all even-power coefficients vanish.

activities.title: Power series intervals & endpoints
activities.description: Explore the series for ln(1+x) and test its boundary values separately.
activities.limits: BC-only unit. Radius is 1; endpoint x=1 converges conditionally, x=−1 diverges.
activities.goal: Explain why the ratio test alone does not decide the endpoints.

activities.title: Infinite limits & asymptotes
activities.description: Compare signed approaches to a vertical asymptote.
activities.equation: f(x)=1/(x−a); opposite sides have opposite infinite limits.
activities.limits: The curve is split at its pole; infinities are behavior descriptions, not finite y-values.
activities.goal: Explain why opposite signed infinite limits do not produce a two-sided infinite limit.

activities.title: Continuity & differentiability
activities.description: Compare the continuous absolute-value curve with its unequal one-sided slopes.
activities.equation: f=scale·|x−a| is continuous but not differentiable at a.
activities.limits: Piecewise linear family; derivative at the corner is undefined.
activities.goal: Explain why continuity is necessary but not sufficient for differentiability.

activities.title: Inverse trigonometric derivatives
activities.description: Compare arcsin x and its derivative on the interior of its domain.
activities.limits: Principal arcsine in radians. Derivative grows without bound near endpoints ±1; endpoints are excluded from finite slope estimates.
activities.goal: Explain the domain restrictions and why the derivative is positive.

activities.title: Related rates: sliding ladder
activities.description: Relate horizontal and vertical endpoint motion for a fixed-length ladder.
activities.limits: Rigid ladder, perpendicular wall and level floor; requires 0<x<L.
activities.goal: Explain why a fixed horizontal rate does not imply a fixed vertical rate.

activities.title: Inflection & concavity tests
activities.description: Separate a change of concavity from a zero second derivative alone.
activities.equation: For x³, f″=6x; for x⁴, f″=12x²
activities.limits: Both have f″(0)=0, but only x³ changes concavity at 0.
activities.goal: Explain why solving f″=0 produces candidates rather than guaranteed inflection points.

activities.title: Trapezoidal approximations & data
activities.description: Approximate a definite integral by connecting sampled values.
activities.limits: Uniform samples; not an exact integral for general curved functions. Error depends on curvature and sampling.
activities.goal: Explain how trapezoids differ from left-rectangle sums.

activities.title: Volumes from cross sections
activities.description: Compare square, semicircular and equilateral-triangle slices across the same base.
activities.equation: Volume=∫cross-section area dx; base width is H−x²
activities.limits: Slices perpendicular to x. Semicircle diameter and triangle side equal the base-region width.
activities.goal: Explain how the same base region can produce different solid volumes.

activities.title: Limit comparison test
activities.description: Compare n/(n²+c) with the harmonic series.
activities.limits: BC-only unit. Both term sequences are positive; a finite positive comparison limit transfers convergence behavior.
activities.goal: Explain why these terms approach zero but their series still diverges.
